title.source: Section check: People, memory and shared histories
title.back: Section check: People, memory and shared histories

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 10–12. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 10–12. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.source: The photo of the covered bridge in Hội An was taken in 2018. What kind of evidence is it?
questions.0.question.note: "covered bridge" is สะพานมีหลังคา. Second pass: checked, SAT10 uses the same words (and mentions สะพานญี่ปุ่น as its popular name); flag removed. The quiz's รูปถ่าย/รูป is now ภาพถ่าย/ภาพ throughout, as in the lessons.
questions.0.question.back: The photo of the covered bridge in Hội An was taken in 2018. What kind of evidence is it?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: A picture of the port in the 1400s
questions.0.options.0.text.back: A picture of the port in the 1400s

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo was taken in 2018, hundreds of years after the port began. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. This picture was taken in 2018, hundreds of years after the port began. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: A view of a place that is still there
questions.0.options.1.text.back: A picture of a place that still stands

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The photo shows the bridge on one day in 2018. It cannot show the old traders.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. This picture shows the bridge on one day in 2018, but cannot show traders from the past.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: A record written by an early trader
questions.0.options.2.text.back: A record written by early traders

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. It is a photo, not a written record. And it was taken in 2018. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is a photo, not a written record, and it was taken in 2018. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.1.question.source: UNESCO describes Hội An's shops, homes and quay. What else could help you learn how people saw the town long ago?
questions.1.question.note: quay is ท่าเทียบเรือ, port ท่าเรือ. Second pass: checked, they match SAT10's glossary; flag removed.
questions.1.question.back: UNESCO describes Hội An's shops, houses and quays. What else would help you know how people in the past saw this town?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: Old records or objects from that time
questions.1.options.0.text.back: Old records or objects from that time

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Buildings show us a place. Old records and objects could help us hear the views of people who lived there.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. Buildings show us the place. Old records and objects might help us hear the views of people who lived there.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: A newer photo of the covered bridge
questions.1.options.1.text.back: A newer photo of the covered bridge

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A new photo shows the bridge today. It cannot show what people thought long ago. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A new photo shows the bridge today. It cannot tell what people in the past thought. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: A longer list of the town's buildings
questions.1.options.2.text.back: A longer list of the town's buildings

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Buildings tell us about the place, not what each person thought. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Buildings tell us about the place, not what each person thought. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.2.question.source: Which question can the 1976 photo of Borobudur help you answer?
questions.2.question.back: Which question can the 1976 photo of Borobudur help you answer?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: What did the first builders plan?
questions.2.options.0.text.back: How did the first builders plan it?
questions.2.options.0.text.note: Second pass: "first builders" is ผู้สร้างกลุ่มแรก, as in SAT11 (was ผู้สร้างรุ่นแรก).

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Borobudur was built in the 700s and 800s. A photo from 1976 cannot show the builders' plans. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.note: "the 700s and 800s" was ช่วงปีคริสต์ศักราช 700 กว่าถึง 800 กว่า. Second pass, one style for centuries across the course: one century is ช่วงปี 1400 ถึง 1499 (KEY_TERMS); a run of two or more is ช่วงปี 1400 ถึง 1800 กว่า ("1400 to 1800-something": accurate to the end of the last century and keeps the English numbers for the checker); late/early is ปลายช่วงปี 700 ถึง 799 / ต้นช่วงปี 900 ถึง 999; picture labels and year labels use a dash (ช่วงปี 1400–1499). Where the English itself says '15th century' (teachers' notes, picture alt) the Thai keeps คริสต์ศตวรรษที่ 15 next to the years. ช่วงปี 1400 alone (which reads as 'around 1400') and ช่วงปีคริสต์ศักราช 700 กว่า are gone. A native speaker should confirm กว่า reads well. Now ช่วงปี 700 ถึง 800 กว่า, as in SAT11; flag removed.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Borobudur was built in the 700-somethings to 800-somethings CE. A photo from 1976 cannot show the builders' plans. Go back to Lesson 11.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: Why did the team choose each repair?
questions.2.options.1.text.back: Why did the team choose to repair each spot that way?

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A photo shows the work, not the reasons for it. Written records or a worker's memories could help. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The photo shows repair work, not reasons. Records or workers' memories might help. Go back to Lesson 11.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: What did the repairs look like?
questions.2.options.2.text.note: "repairs" is งานซ่อม (everyday), not การบูรณะ (restoration), to keep the option as plain as the others.
questions.2.options.2.text.back: What did the repair work look like?

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The photo records one moment of modern conservation work, in 1976.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. This picture records one moment of modern conservation work, in 1976.

questions.3.question.source: The Borobudur team kept its photos, drawings and notes. People can study them later. What is a set of records like this called?
questions.3.question.note: "drawings" is ภาพลายเส้น (the lesson's "as-built drawings").
questions.3.question.back: The Borobudur team kept their photos, line drawings and records so people could study them later. What is a collection of records like this called?

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A stupa is a bell-shaped tower on the monument. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.note: stupa is สถูป; "bell-shaped tower" is สิ่งก่อสร้างรูประฆัง; "monument" is โบราณสถาน (KEY_TERMS, a large old structure).
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A stupa is a bell-shaped structure on this monument. Go back to Lesson 11.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. An archive keeps records safe. Later, people can compare them and ask why each repair was made.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. An archive keeps records safe. Later people can compare those records and ask why each spot was repaired that way.

questions.3.options.2.text.note: "recognition" was การยกย่อง. Second pass: now การรับรอง, SAT11's glossary word (the lesson says ยูเนสโกรับรอง), in the option and its feedback; flag removed.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Recognition is when a group says something is important. In 2017, UNESCO said this about the archive. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Recognition is when a group says something is important. In 2017 UNESCO said this about this archive. Go back to Lesson 11.

questions.4.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A class makes a small exhibit about the made-up town of Nolbe. Panel 1 has a photo of an old stone well. The class needs to write a credit under the photo.
questions.4.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A class made a small exhibition about a made-up town called Nolbe. Panel 1 has a photo of an old stone well. The class must write a credit under the picture.

questions.4.question.source: Which line is the best credit for the photo?
questions.4.question.back: Which text is the best credit for this picture?

questions.4.options.0.text.note: Credit line written without commas (Thai style): ภาพ: Ana Bello ปี 2021 ห้องสมุด Nolbe. Names kept in Latin letters.

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A credit says who made the source, when, and where it is kept. Then others can check it.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. A credit says who made this source, when, and where it is kept, so others can check.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Every person in Nolbe used this well
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Everyone in Nolbe used this well.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. This is a claim about the past, and the photo cannot prove it. A credit says who made the source. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. This is a claim about the past, and the photo cannot prove it. A credit says who made this source. Go back to Lesson 12.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: This is the best photo in our exhibit
questions.4.options.2.text.back: This is the best picture in our exhibition.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This is an opinion. A credit names who made the source and where it is kept. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is an opinion. A credit names who made the source and where it is kept. Go back to Lesson 12.

questions.5.question.source: Your two sources do not show what local people thought. What should you do in your exhibit?
questions.5.question.back: Your two sources do not show what local people thought. What should you do in your exhibition?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Make up what local people said
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Make up what local people said

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A fair exhibit does not invent evidence. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A fair exhibition does not make up evidence. Go back to Lesson 12.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: Leave the gap out, so it looks complete
questions.5.options.1.text.back: Don't mention the gap, so it looks complete

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Hiding a gap makes the story look more certain than it is. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Hiding a gap makes the story look more certain than the truth. Go back to Lesson 12.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Say that this perspective is missing
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Say that this point of view is missing

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. A fair account can say, "This source does not tell us." Then visitors know what is still unsure.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. A fair account can say, "This source does not tell us," and then visitors will know what is still uncertain.

results.high.source: Well done. You know how places, records and exhibits can tell a history fairly.
results.high.back: Great work. You know how places, records and exhibitions can tell history fairly.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Well done. You got many right. Go back to the lessons for the questions you have not got right yet, then try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 10–12, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 10–12 and try again. Take as long as you need.
